Q: What are the available approaches for binary obfuscation in iOS apps (Swift + Objective-C)? A:

I've worked for 2 different financial institutions that both used app hardening/code obfuscation as part of their automated build process. They used commercial tools that alter the code generation process during the release build process. I am blanking on the names of the products at the moment, and we aren't really supposed to recommend third party tools in these forums anyway.

I wasn't that involved in the automated build process so I didn't interact with these tools much. They did occasionally introduce obscure runtime bugs, but that was fairly rare.

Q: Why there are empty spaces in the middle of the string returned by re.split()? A:

In addition to the other good explanatory Answers, you may find it's easier to design your regex to take matches of runs of not-delimiters rather than splitting

>>> re.findall(r"[^!\s]+", "Hello! How are you?")
['Hello', 'How', 'are', 'you?']

Or if you want a collection of both, expressly giving a group to both words and delimiters

>>> d = r"!\s"
>>> re.findall(fr"([^{d}]+|[{d}]+)", "Hello! How are you?")
['Hello', '! ', 'How', ' ', 'are', ' ', 'you?']

>>> [m.groups() for m in re.finditer(fr"([^{d}]+)([{d}]*)", "Hello! How are you?")]
[('Hello', '! '), ('How', ' '), ('are', ' '), ('you?', '')]
>>> list(zip(*_))  # unzip groups
[('Hello', 'How', 'are', 'you?'), ('! ', ' ', ' ', '')]

Q: <3>WSL (358) ERROR: CreateProcessParseCommon:789: Failed to translate Z:/ A:

I had a similar error on my Ubuntu 25.10 running on WSL

ERROR: CreateProcessParseCommon:996: getpwnam() failed 17

My /etc/wsl.conf had this line :

[user]
default =

I removed the spaces around "=" and replaced the line with the following line followed by a wsl restart which solved the issue.

default=<username>

Q: How would i sign a user out once the jwt token expires in react? A:

Although approach demonstrated by Jawad Ahbab is more robust considering your scenario, I want to counter-ask the following:

Is it a requirement to logout user exactly on token expiry?

Because if it is OK to delay sign out process, then you can put a handler for requests to your backend. So when requests (any request) are failing with 401 response status code (or any other response status code you backend returns for invalid/expired tokens) then your frontend will clear the localStorage and redirect user to log in page.

While this approach will most of the time wait for user's action until your frontend realizes token has been expired (by sending request to backend), you never repeat the expiry calculation logic on frontend as it is surely already done in backend.

Additionally, I think most of the client side applications send couple of requests to BE even if user is idle (to refresh page state etc.), so in this case your user will be logged out much earlier. Although it is just an assumption.

Also, I would recommend using session storage for token's, not local storage.

Q: Why do I get a syntax error when I try to use a parameter in my query? A:

Use mysqli::prepare, not query to prepare your prepared statement.

query will try to run that query which isn't valid until the parameters have been bound.

Q: How to reshape from long to wide format filling NAs with zeros A:

1) Sticking with the framework in the question replace each NA in the input with NaN. Then we can distinguish the type of missing value as NaN (missing value coming from input) or NA (missing value resulting from reshape):

res <- reshape(
  replace(df, is.na(df), NaN),
  idvar = "ID",
  timevar = "region",
  direction = "wide"
)
res

##   ID status.A status.B
## 1  1        1      NaN
## 3  2        1        1
## 5  3      NaN       NA

If it is important that the original NA's be NA and the ones from reshape are 0 then add this:

res[is.na(res) & !is.nan(as.matrix(res))] <- 0
res[is.na(res)] <- NA

2) In the question's example we only have 1 and NA in the status column so if those are the only possibilities we could represent status using a logical variable instead in which case the entire problem goes away:

reshape(
  transform(df, status = !is.na(status)),
  idvar = "ID",
  timevar = "region",
  direction = "wide"
)

##   ID status.A status.B
## 1  1     TRUE    FALSE
## 3  2     TRUE     TRUE
## 5  3    FALSE       NA

3) We could use tapply from base R as it has a default argument. It returns a matrix ta so if that is ok we are done. If a data frame is needed then use the second line as well.

ta <- tapply(df[[3]], df[-3], c, default = 0)
data.frame(ID = rownames(ta), ta, row.names = NULL)

##   ID  A  B
## 1  1  1 NA
## 2  2  1  1
## 3  3 NA  0

4) Yet another base R approach is xtabs where ftable2df is from Reshaping an array to data.frame and only uses base R. If an xtabs object is ok only the first leg of the pipeline is needed or if an ftable object is ok then only the first two legs.

xtabs(status ~., df) |> ftable() |> ftable2df()

##   ID  A  B
## 1  1  1 NA
## 2  2  1  1
## 3  3 NA  0
